current_example.title: Example: Computing 4x4 Determinants Using Row and Column Operations

q-91173.name: Question 1
q-91173.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above ${a}_{44}$ equal to zero.*
q-91173.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 5 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 2 & 2 \\ 5 & 3 & 4 & -2 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{4} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{4} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+2{R}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 14 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 & 0 \\ 9 & 3 & 10 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 14 & 0 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 & 0 \\ 9 & 3 & 10 & 0 \\ 2 & 0 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 14 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 \\ 9 & 3 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}5 & -2 & 14 \\ -3 & -1 & -4 \\ 9 & 3 & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

q-131255.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{22}=2$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & -6 & -11 & -5 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 2 & 4 & -1 & 5 \\ -3 & -2 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 4 & 7 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 0 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-7 & 0 & 4 & 7 \\ -3 & 2 & 5 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 0 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 7 \\ 8 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}-7 & 4 & 7 \\ 8 & -11 & -3 \\ -6 & 6 & 2\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

q-42930.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}|

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries above and below ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero.*
q-42930.worked_solution:
Let's make entries above and below ${a}_{33}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -2 & 5 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 3 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+{R}_{3} \\ {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{3} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 3 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & 7 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 1 \\ 2 & 7 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}2 & 6 & 0 \\ -4 & -7 & 1 \\ 2 & 7 & 8\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

q-91170.name: Question 5
q-91170.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary row operations to make the entries below ${a}_{12}$ equal to zero.*
q-91170.worked_solution:
Let's make entries below ${a}_{12}=-1$ equal to zero using elementary row operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 2 & 3 & 5 & 2 \\ -3 & -1 & 3 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\ {R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\ {R}_{4}:={R}_{4}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd column, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 4 & 3 \\ 11 & 0 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 0 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{1+2}|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}11 & 17 & 11 \\ -6 & -1 & -1 \\ 11 & 7 & 7\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

q-91221.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left of ${a}_{44}$ equal to zero.*
q-91221.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left of ${a}_{44}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -3 & -1 \\ -2 & -3 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 1 & 4 & -2 \\ 4 & -2 & 3 & 1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-4){C}_{4} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{4} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{4}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & -1 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 & 2 \\ 11 & -3 & 10 & -2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 \\ 11 & -3 & 10\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ -10 & 1 & -5 \\ 11 & -3 & 10\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

q-91220.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}|
$$

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}$ equal to zero.*
q-91220.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{33}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-2 & -4 & 2 & 1 \\ 3 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 6 & -4 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 & -3\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-3){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+(-1){C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $3$rd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & 2 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 0 \\ 8 & -7 & -2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2|\begin{aligned}-8 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 4 & 1 \\ 8 & -7 & -1\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 12 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 1 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}|

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{21}$ equal to zero.*
q-132020.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{21}=2$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & 6 & 12 & -5 \\ 2 & 4 & 6 & -4 \\ -3 & 1 & -8 & 2 \\ 5 & 2 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-2){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+2{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 7 & 1 & -4 \\ 5 & -8 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $2$nd row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}4 & -2 & 0 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -3 & 7 & 1 & -4 \\ 5 & -8 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{2+1}|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 3 \\ 7 & 1 & -4 \\ -8 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 & 3 \\ 7 & 1 & -4 \\ -8 & -10 & 4\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 9 & -2 & 7 \\ 5 & 3 & 6 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}|

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the right of ${a}_{41}$ equal to zero.*
q-132023.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the right of ${a}_{41}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 & 7 & -5 \\ -2 & 9 & -2 & 7 \\ 5 & 3 & 6 & 6 \\ 1 & -2 & 3 & -1\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+2{C}_{1} \\ {C}_{3}:={C}_{3}+(-3){C}_{1} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+{C}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 5 & 13 & -9 & 11 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $4$th row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}3 & 7 & -2 & -2 \\ -2 & 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 5 & 13 & -9 & 11 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+1}|\begin{aligned}7 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 13 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}7 & -2 & -2 \\ 5 & 4 & 5 \\ 13 & -9 & 11\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

q-91219.problem:
$$
|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -4 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}|

Consider the above $4\times 4$ determinant. Which of the following $3\times 3$ determinants has the same value?

*Hint: Use elementary column operations to make the entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{13}$ equal to zero.*
q-91219.worked_solution:
Let's make entries to the left and to the right of ${a}_{13}=1$ equal to zero using elementary column operations.

Since adding a multiple of one row (or column) to another row (column) in a matrix does not change the value of its determinant, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -4 \\ -4 & 2 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & -2 & -1 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & -2 & 2\end{aligned}| &  & \,\begin{aligned}{C}_{1}:={C}_{1}+(-1){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{2}:={C}_{2}+(-3){C}_{3} \\ {C}_{4}:={C}_{4}+4{C}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -6 & -4 & 2 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the result along the $1$st row, we get

$$
\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -6 & -4 & 2 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -2 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}-6 & -4 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-6 & -4 & 9 \\ 6 & 1 & -1 \\ 9 & 5 & -6\end{aligned}|.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned} & \,\,|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & -3 & 0 & 5 \\ 3 & -8 & -3 & 2 \\ -3 & 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 5 \\ -8 & -3 & 2 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 & 5 \\ -8 & -3 & 2 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-3)\cdot (-1)^{2+2}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 5 \\ 9 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-3(3-45) \\  & =126.\end{aligned}
$$
